key_insight: DMA² shows that distribution matching for few-step image generation works better in native RGB pixel space when training is split into two complementary objectives: a fixed high-noise teacher-matching band and adversarial/anchor guidance. This reveals that low-noise RGB matching is overly dominated by local texture cues, so the method deliberately reshapes how the model learns fine detail.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the gap between modern DMD-style few-step distillation and pixel-space image generation. Existing text-to-image distillation methods are built mostly around latent diffusion, which misses key properties of native RGB and can learn poor matching behavior at low noise levels.
method: Revisits two DMD interfaces for pixel-space teachers to understand where standard matching breaks down.
Introduces a fixed high-noise matching band for teacher matching, avoiding the overemphasis on local textures seen in low-noise RGB.
Adds adversarial and anchor losses to better align generated images with the target distribution while preserving stable structure and detail.
impact: For practitioners, this work offers a more principled way to distill fast image generators directly in pixel space. It can improve few-step generation quality without relying on latent-space assumptions, making RGB-native pipelines more effective and easier to analyze.
